To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel approach for discovering research interests based on users' interactions with articles, that we show that this approach outperforms a text-based topic modelling approach in terms of coherence and interpretability of the topics and that we show the validity of our approach in terms of recommendation performance.

we present an effective solution to discover coherent and interpretable topics of interest in Mendeley, that leverages the interactions between users, articles and keywords, and that outperforms state-of-the-art text-based topic modelling approaches.

we propose a topic model that leverages the interactions between users' research interests, articles and their content to discover coherent research topics that are more easily interpretable and that we evaluate this approach using a research interest prediction and article recommendation task.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of identifying users' research topics from their article collections in Mendeley, and we propose a novel three-step approach that leverages the interactions between users, articles and keywords in the Mendeley platform to discover coherent and interpretable topics.

the problem of discovering users' interests from their interactions with scholarly articles and the proposed solution provides a novel approach for topic modelling and research interest identification that is effective in different research disciplines and can be easily adapted to other recommendation scenarios.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed method is a promising approach to infer research topics and interests of users, and that the method is able to provide a good compromise between interpretability and performance in the considered recommendation tasks.
the topic model based on user interactions with articles is a valid approach to discover users' research interests.
our approach provides a valid and effective way to discover users' research interests, with the added benefits of interpretability and the ability to handle different research disciplines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach is able to effectively identify research interests of users in different research disciplines, which is a key component of scholarly reference management systems.
we present a new way of discovering users' interests based on the articles they have added to Mendeley, and that this approach is more effective than text-based topic models.

we propose a topic modelling method for research interests discovery that can be used to provide recommendations of relevant articles to users and to organise information in large digital repositories, such as the Mendeley dataset, and that is interpretable and effective for different research disciplines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reference management data can be effectively leveraged for inferring users' research interests and providing recommendations in a personalised way.

the reference management data available in platforms such as Mendeley provides a good source of information for discovering users' research topics, which can be used for providing personalised recommendations.

a topic model based only on the interactions between articles and users can provide coherent topics of interest that are easily interpretable and that are effective in predicting users' research interests and recommending articles.
